Bournemouth moved a step closer to automatic qualification for the Europa League last 16 after coming from behind with 10 men to win 2-1 at Celta Vigo .
It was a remarkable 10th victory in a row in all competitions for Marco Rose’s side and it might have been the most satisfying of the lot for the manager, coming as it did after his team had found themselves a goal down and a man down at half-time.
The visitors looked in trouble when, minutes after Iago Aspas had curled Celta in front, Bafodé Diakité was red-carded for a poorly timed tackle.
Bournemouth might have folded then, but instead they came roaring back, Álvaro Rodríguez heading them level almost immediately after the start of the second half. A draw would have been an excellent result in the circumstances. Substitute Rayan had other ideas, waiting at the end of a rapid breakaway to sweep in the winner 12 minutes from time. Rose’s team could secure a top-eight finish and a last-16 berth when they host Viktoria Plzen , 4-0 winners over Benfica , in two weeks’ time.
Camilo Durán came to Celtic ’s rescue in Europe again after coming off the bench to head a late winner against Torreense in Portugal.
The Colombian striker peeled off to the back post to meet a cross from fellow substitute James Forrest and send a downward header into the net in the 85th minute. Durán’s 15th goal of the season earned a 2-1 victory over the Portuguese second-tier side and put Celtic on six points in the Europa League after his double off the bench inspired a comeback win over Besiktas last time out.
Celtic took the lead in the ninth minute when Javi Vázquez sliced Jota’s cross into his own net with Yang Hyun-jun right behind him. But the Portuguese Cup winners levelled 10 minutes later after some sloppy defending. Both Kieran Tierney and Colby Donovan had chances to deal with bouncing balls after Álex Alfaro hit the bar from 22 yards but they could not clear and Haiti international Dany Jean volleyed home.
Celtic dominated second-half possession but clear chances were at a premium until Durán struck. Torreense sit 13th in the Portuguese second tier and hosted Celtic in Leiria, 60 miles away from their home town. Hoops fans formed the vast majority of the 4,971 crowd. But the hosts started the game three points ahead of Celtic after wins over Lillestrøm and Ararat-Armenia, and they had taken the lead against Sunderland before the Premier League side netted a stoppage-time winner.
The lead-up to Marseille against Levski Sofia was marred by incidents in the stands between supporters, including the throwing of projectiles and flares. Several Marseille fans ran from the stand about 10 minutes before kick-off, appearing to pursue a group of Bulgarian supporters. They breached the stand designated for away fans, where around 500 Levski supporters were gathered.
Security personnel eventually managed to restore calm as the game kicked off on time. Five people were taken to hospital with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder,” the Marseille police prefecture said. sSix others were treated on site for various wounds. The home team went on to win the game 1-0 thanks to a first-half Amine Gouiri penalty.
Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler hailed a “very impressive” impact from Ibrahim Osman after his first goals for the club helped secure a 4-0 success over 10-man Universitatea Craiova .
Winger Osman finished a flowing team move to give Albion a third-minute lead at the Amex Stadium before Maxim De Cuyper superbly curled home his fifth goal of the campaign to double the advantage.
Romanian champions Craiova were left with little hope of a comeback when defender Vladimir Screciu was sent off in the 39th minute for stamping on the ankle of Matt O’Riley.
Ghana international Osman set up Charalampos Kostoulas for the third goal before quickly claiming his second with a fine individual effort as the Seagulls made it 10 points from four games in the competition.
“He showed a really good performance today,” said head coach Hurzeler. “This is very helpful to have these one-against-one players. He showed a very impressive style today.”
The 21-year-old is yet to start a Premier League game for Brighton but now has two goals and three assists in four Conference League outings this term after impressing Hurzeler in pre-season.
Hearts ’ Conference League hopes suffered a hammer blow as Folarin Balogun’s stoppage-time goal consigned them to a 3-2 defeat at home to Monaco .
The Jambos looked on course to pick up their second league-phase point after stunning first-half strikes from Jordi Altena and Sabah Kerjota either side of goals from visiting pair Folarin Balogun and Edian Diop.
But in the last of four added minutes, USA forward Balogun got himself free in the box to slot home and maintain Monaco’s perfect record in the competition.
Hearts will now require high-scoring victories over Borac and Pafos in their last two games to have a chance of scrambling into the top 24 and qualifying for the knockout phase.
Ruben Amorim’s Milan , who had lost three of their opening four matches, gave their hopes of avoiding an embarrassing early exit a boost with a 4-2 victory at Olympiakos .
Milan were facing another huge blow to their bid to reach the knockout phase when they were trailing to a Mike Maignan own goal and Jota Silva’s 49th-minute strike. Omari Hutchinson’s brilliant solo goal gave Milan a lifeline, and the winger then set up Alphadjo Cisse to equalise in the 63rd minute.
Hutchinson added another assist as he crossed for Christian Pulisic to volley home 19 minutes from time, before Diego Moreira’s injury-time fourth.
Juventus shrugged off an early scare to cruise past Cypriots Omonia Nicosia and move closer to confirming a top-eight place in the Europa League with a 4-1 win in Turin.
The Italian giants fell behind to a 15th-minute strike from Lubomir Satka but levelled through Andrea Cambiaso before further goals from Jeff Ekhator, Francisco Conceiçao and Jeremie Boga earned a comfortable win. Only Bournemouth sit above Juve in the table.
Bayer Leverkusen also remained in contention for automatic progression after second-half strikes from Malik Tillman and Jarell Quansah secured a 2-0 win at Dinamo Zagreb . Hoffenheim secured their second win in this season’s competition by beating Sturm Graz 3-1.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new deal until the summer of 2029 at Leeds; the striker joined the club in 2025 from Everton; he has scored six goals in all competitions this season; his form earned him a recall to the England squad
Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new deal at Leeds, keeping him at the club until the summer of 2029.
Sky Sports News has been reporting that he was expected to commit his future to the club, which has now been confirmed.
Calvert-Lewin joined Leeds on a free transfer in the summer of 2025 after leaving Everton. He scored 15 goals across all competitions last season, and has scored six this season. He scored in a 4-1 win against Chelsea on Saturday.
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Since he joined Leeds, Calvert-Lewin is the highest-scoring Englishman in the Premier League (19) - three ahead of his next closest countrymen, Morgan Gibbs-White and Ollie Watkins.
His form for Leeds saw him return to the England set-up in March, and he also featured in the September/October and November squads. Calvert-Lewin was not selected for the World Cup.
Ao Tanaka is also close to signing a new contract with Leeds, Sky Sports News understands.
The midfielder is understood to have agreed terms on a deal that will keep him at Elland Road until 2029. The 28-year-old's current contract was due to expire in the summer of 2028.
Tanaka has grown to become a key figure in Daniel Farke's side this season, starting in nine of Leeds' 11 Premier League matches. They have lost just 10 of the 66 games Tanaka has started since then.
Calvert-Lewin follows in the footsteps of Ethan Ampadu, Joe Rodon, Jayden Bogle and Brenden Aaronson, who all signed new deals in the summer. Leeds are also reportedly set to trigger Lukas Nmecha's one-year extension.
Leeds are seventh in the Premier League, four points from the Champions League places. They face Coventry next in the league on Saturday.
Ahead of the weekend's match, Daniel Farke has refused to shed any more light on his own new contract talks. He signed a four-year contract when appointed in 2023 and that is set to expire at the end of the season.
He was reported to have parted company with his agent in October while reaching an agreement with Leeds in principle to extend his contract until 2029.
Farke said: "I'm the manager of Leeds United. I sign players. I don't sign managers. Since I've been here, I fell in love with the people here, and I fell in love with the club.
"And the only thing I care for is our supporters because they had to suffer really for such a long time. I want to bring success to them. I care for the players, I care for the staff and this is the way I work.
"I think this is also the reason I don't like to talk about my contract at all because I have to lead the people here.
"I'm a leader of men and women at this club and and no one wants a leader who talks about his future, about himself, or whatever. And this also not my style."

Wesley Fofana played all 90 minutes of Chelsea's 4-1 defeat at home to Leeds United on Saturday
Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso says defender Wesley Fofana has apologised for a controversial interview he gave on YouTube.
Fofana has been criticised for comments he made in the interview with YouTuber Zach Nani in which he appeared to joke about his penalty miss in a Carabao Cup shootout defeat at Liverpool .
He did not have permission to hold the two-hour interview, which was aired after Chelsea 's humiliating 4-1 defeat at home to rivals Leeds on Saturday, but Alonso said the matter was now "closed".
"It was unfortunate. He has apologised. He knows it was not right, the moment, it was not right, the content," said the Blues boss, who was speaking before Friday's Premier League match at Nottingham Forest .
"We are here to take things seriously. He's said it will not be repeated. We don't want these kind of things and they won't be repeated."
Alonso refused to confirm whether Fofana had been punished by the club, but said "we have addressed that with him."
'Fragile' and 'miles off it' - Alonso's Chelsea honeymoon is over
Fofana's comments followed criticism from fans of his performances this season, including in last weekend's humiliation at the hands of historic rivals Leeds .
But interviewer Nani defended Fofana against the backlash, saying: "People can clearly see he wasn't happy. He admits he didn't play well and says he needs to improve."
The interviewer also defended Fofana's explanation for putting himself forward to take a penalty against Liverpool , saying the defender believed it was his responsibility as one of the senior players on the pitch.
The 25-year-old France defender has often struggled for form and fitness since completing a £70m move from Leicester City in August 2022.
He has made 81 appearances for the club in four years, but has played nine times under new manager Alonso this season.
In that time Chelsea have struggled with defensive frailty, conceding 20 goals in their 11 Premier League games.
They are eighth in the table after falling to a third defeat in their last four league matches.

Authorities rescued 17 crew members but one later died in hospital after a diesel tanker capsized off the Spanish island of Ibiza. A contingency plan against possible pollution damage is now in place.
A tanker carrying up to 7,000 metric tonnes (7,716 short tons) of diesel capzized off the Spanish island of Ibiza, local authorities said on Thursday.
The ship's 17 crew members were rescued but one later died in hospital and another six suffered from hypothermia when the Maltese-flagged Med Emre capsized overnight, the government of Spain's Balearic Islands, said in a statement.
According to emergency services, the five further crew members were taken to Valencia and the remainig five were in good condition on a ‌rescue ​vessel.
The chemical tanker was sailing from Algeciras to Barcelona when it capsized about 30 nautical miles (56 kilometers) off Ibiza's northwestern coast.
According to Spanish authorities, the Med Emre was drifting upside down northwest of Ibiza after capsizing. Initially, they said the ship had sunk to the seabed in 1,000 metres of water, but later corrected this statement.
The nationalities of the crew or the cause of the incident was not immediately clear.
The Transport Ministry said the maritime rescue vessel Guardamar Talia had reported no wreckage, floating debris or signs of pollution at the site as of Thursday morning. It added that another rescue ship was heading to the area to continue monitoring the situation.
Spain's maritime rescue service deployed an aircraft and the Clara Campoamor, a vessel equipped to respond to oil spills, to inspect the area.
Spain's merchant marine authority ​has activated the national maritime pollution contingency plan at level 2, the second-highest.
The Balearic regional government said it was assessing the incident and its potential impact, including the risk of fuel pollution, before deciding on further measures.
The waters surrounding Ibiza are a critical zone for biodiversity as they host sea turtles, dolphins and the ‌Balearic shearwater, one of Europe's most threatened seabirds.
The area also hosts vast Posidonia oceanica seagrass meadows, which are essential for maintaining marine biodiversity.
Emilio Rodriguez Diaz, a maritime security expert at the University of Cadiz, told Cadena SER radio that the area affected was "particularly vulnerable."
But he said the Med Emre was a modern ship, built in Turkey in 2019, with a double hull to ensure that, "in the event of a leak (or) a collision, that intermediate part between the cargo hold and the outer layer would flood."
"It's a kind of buffer that prevents the cargo... from being released into the environment," he said.
Spain's worst maritime environmental disaster happened in 2022, when the tanker Prestige sank off the northwestern Galicia region. It spilled tens of thousands of heavy fuel oil and polluted beaches across Spain and France.

texts.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/art:
Marco Rose replaced Andoni Iraola - who ended up at Liverpool - in the summer
Bournemouth are dreaming of winning the Europa League after staging a 10-man fightback to join a select band of teams to win their first five European games.
The Cherries trailed 1-0 to Iago Aspas' goal at Celta Vigo, and then went down to 10 men midway through the first half when Bafode Diakite was sent off.
But second-half goals from Alvaro Rodriguez and Rayan gave the Cherries a 10th consecutive win in all competitions, extending their club record run.
Bournemouth are only the third side to win each of their first five European matches (excluding qualifiers and including the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup), after Nuremberg in 1961-62 and Ararat in 1972-73.
They top this season's table as the only club to win five out of five - and are closing in on a top-eight spot, which would mean they skip a play-off round and go straight into the last 16.
Some fans have told the BBC they have already booked hotels in Frankfurt for the final on 26 May.
As supporters sang about reaching that game, midfielder Alex Scott was asked for his thoughts on TNT Sports.
"Of course that's our dream. When you grow up wanting to be a footballer you dream of winning trophies," Scott said.
"Where this club has come from to where it is now, full credit to everyone who has built it.
"For players, it's a dream to be on the pitch playing for this club. We have still got wins to get to qualify into the top eight, and from there all focus is on pushing forward and hopefully we can go on and win it."
The Cherries are in unprecedented times, with their biggest trophy to date being when they won the second-tier Championship in 2014-15.
In terms of cups, they won the 1983–84 Associate Members' Cup - which later became the EFL Trophy.
Head coach Marco Rose, who replaced Andoni Iraola in the summer, said: "It's always allowed to dream.
"If you get a competition like this you want to achieve the best possible thing. We know it's far away to go. Many games. Now it's about getting into the top eight to avoid more games and then we can see step by step."
As well as just winning their games, Bournemouth are firing in the goals. They have netted at least twice in each match during this 10-game winning run.
And they are the first side to score at least twice in each of their first five matches in Europe since Queens Park Rangers in 1976.
The win on Thursday was made even more impressive by the fact they contested 75% of the game with 10 men.
It came days after Manchester United seemed to implode after an early red card against Liverpool , losing 4-0.
Former England manager Glenn Hoddle said on TNT: "They have deserved this result. They've played beautifully with 10 men - probably as good as I've seen a team play defensively and with the ball.
"I've not seen a team go down to 10 men for so long and dictate a game and deserve to win the game. They were absolutely brilliant."
Cherries boss Rose told BBC Radio Solent: "What a team, what a spirit, what an energy.
"I said to Ty [Tyler Adams] sometimes it's not about tactics and formations and stuff like this. [David] Brooks did a great job when we got one player less - he played right defender like he played it for 10 years. We changed in the right moment. Everyone did his job on a really high level.
"We were just relentless and we never stopped to believe in this win and that's why big, big, big congratulations to the team.
"You feel if you're one player down that it's a difficult night, but to handle a difficult night like this, it just shows the character of the team and of the whole group."
The coach's belief in what they are doing filters through to the players.
Amine Adli, who set up the equaliser, told the BBC: "At half-time, everyone still believed we can turn the game in our way and this is what happened.
"Everyone was like 'guys we can make it, we have to believe. If we score the game can change.'"
Earlier this month, the attacking midfielder said he saw a lot of similarities to the Bayer Leverkusen team he was part of in 2023-24.
That is not a bad comparison, considering they went unbeaten to win the domestic double, as well as reaching the Europa League final.

Real Madrid'in resmi açıklamasına göre XM Label, kadro içinde en çok seçilen araç oldu. Plug-in hibrit modelde V8 benzinli motor, elektrik motoruyla birlikte çalışıyor ve toplam 748 beygir güç üretiyor.
BMW XM Label'ın Almanya 'daki liste fiyatı 183 bin 400 euro. Euro kurunun 55,5 TL civarında seyrettiği bu günlerde araç yaklaşık 10,2 milyon TL'ye denk geliyor.
Takım bu sezon BMW'nin en geniş araç ve motor seçeneğine sahip. XM Label'ın yanı sıra tam elektrikli BMW iX3 50 xDrive de en çok seçilen modeller arasında yer aldı. iX3 50 xDrive, 805 kilometreye kadar menzil sunuyor.
Lüks sedan BMW i7 60 xDrive ise tamamen elektrikli sürüş sunuyor ve 727 kilometreye kadar menzile ulaşabiliyor.

Hearts lost 3-2 at home to Monaco in the Conference League; Jordi Altena opened the scoring; Sabah Kerjota pulled the Jambos back level after goals from Folarin Balogun and Edan Diop; Balogun netted again in stoppage-time; the Jambos have one point from their opening four games
Wouter Vrancken expressed pride in his Hearts team after an agonising 3-2 defeat at home to Monaco left their Conference League hopes hanging by a thread.
The Jambos looked on course to pick up their second league-phase point after stunning first-half strikes from Jordi Altena and Sabah Kerjota either side of goals from visiting pair Folarin Balogun and Edian Diop.
But in the fourth and final minute of added time, injury-hit Hearts were denied what would have been a hugely commendable result when USA forward Balogun found space in the box to slot home and maintain Monaco's perfect record in the competition.
"The biggest thing is, of course, to be really proud of the performance we put on the park today, because it's against a really good side," said Vrancken, keen to reiterate that his team remains without several key players.
"Knowing that we have still nine injuries, I will mention it, and we have a lot of players not on the European list today and to still do this against that team, I'm really proud of what we did."
A point would have significantly boosted Hearts' hopes of reaching the knockout phase, but they can now only finish on a maximum of seven points - the same tally they managed two years ago before being eliminated on goal difference under Neil Critchley.
With their goal difference currently standing at minus five, Hearts will likely need high-scoring victories against Bosnian side Borac and Cypriot outfit Pafos in their final two matches to stand a chance of breaking into the top 24 and extending their European campaign beyond Christmas.
Vrancken, however, does not believe the late goal will make a significant difference to his side's prospects.
"I think the point doesn't make a difference," he said. "One or no points doesn't change anything in the next games. There's also something that really was pleasing for me, that when it was 2-2, we still wanted to go.
"We wanted to go for the win here, and against a side like this, in the situation we're in, so really proud of this also, because three points would make a difference.
"Zero or one point doesn't make a difference towards the next games, so you have to win the next games." Vrancken believes the quality of the goals scored by Altena and Kerjota, both exquisite finishes from range, highlighted the renewed belief coursing through his squad after their 8-0 win over Dundee last weekend.
"They were quality goals," he said. "You see the confidence those guys have, and this is what we wanted after the weekend, of course, that you take some confidence of the dynamics we did there.
"I think the conviction around the box was there, also in both boxes actually. It's an important thing to take with us towards the next games coming, especially in this run of games."

Your questions answered by Sky Sports News' James Savundra on Chelsea's season, with Blues having lost three of last four in Premier League; Wesley Fofana’s unauthorised interview, the absences of Danny Welbeck and Estevao, and January transfer plans all addressed
After Chelsea fell to back-to-back losses with a 4-1 humiliation by Leeds at Stamford Bridge last Saturday, Sky Sports News reporter James Savundra examines the latest developments at Stamford Bridge.
As well as suffering a third defeat in four Premier League games, Chelsea and manager Xabi Alonso also faced the added frustration of defender Wesley Fofana giving an unauthorised interview this week, in which he laughed off his penalty miss in last month's Carabao Cup defeat to Liverpool and revealed he had contemplated retiring during his time at Stamford Bridge.
Here, Savundra addresses Fofana's future, Joao Pedro's injury, transfer plans and much more...
Jake: Is Fofana expected to face any disciplinary action for his impromptu interview? Some of the things said in that were unacceptable from a footballer, especially one involved in as much off-the-pitch controversy as him.
James says: Xabi Alonso addressed this at Thursday's press conference. Fofana has apologised following the interview. The matter has been dealt with internally and there are no suggestions that the defender is set to miss any matches.
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Whether the club look to punish Fofana with a fine is not known at this stage. Alonso made clear that this will not be repeated. It's completely understandable to emphasise with Chelsea supporters. Fofana simply hasn't justified the £75m that Chelsea paid Leicester City.
Benny: Why is Fofana still being chosen when every single fan watching football can see how poor his form is?
James says: At the moment there is a lack of real alternative options. Xabi Alonso stood behind the Fofana-Colwill axis during Thursday's press conference despite their clear struggles dealing with Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Brian Brobbey.
Liam Delap will prove a similar physical threat tomorrow [Friday] with an added point to prove. Ultimately, Chelsea trimmed down their squad in the summer in light of no European football. Maxence Lacroix would be starting, possibly ahead of Fofana right now if he was fit.
Colwill has found things difficult this season having missed the majority of the last campaign. In hindsight, should Chelsea have sold Trevoh Chalobah? Perhaps it was time for the academy graduate to end his Chelsea chapter but he rarely let the side down.
You could feasibly play Josh Acheampong at centre-back. The youngster has been a shining light this season. Yet he looks comfortable on the right. Do you want to upset something which actually seems to be working. And if Acheampong moves to centre-back, then does Marco Palestra play as a right-back?
The Italian impressed in Serie A as a wing-back but with Chelsea opting largely for a flat back four, is Palestra defensively good enough to fulfil that role. Aaron Anselmino remains an option but hasn't played a minute for the club this season.
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso of Wesley Fofana: "We have addressed that with him and for sure it was unfortunate. He has apologised. He knows it wasn't the right moment. The content wasn't right. "We are here to take things seriously and he said it wouldn't be repeated. We know it's something we don't want and they are not going to be repeated."
Mikey: Will Chelsea sell and buy any defenders and strikers in January? I feel we need stronger defenders with a better aerial ability and maybe a more out and out No 9 to challenge Joao Pedro and give us something different.
James says: Chelsea will spend money in January if they believe it will help them achieve their target this season - qualifying for the Champions League. They were pleased with what they did in the summer but accept that the squad still requires investment.
It seems unlikely any defenders will be sold given the lack of current options. A loan move would seem to suit Aaron Anselmino given his lack of options. The winter window is a difficult one. There's a sense that Chelsea could benefit from signing a more experienced centre-back, considering the moves for Emi Martinez, Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck in every other area of the pitch in the summer.
The club have shown a willingness to tweak their transfer model and sign players for the here and now, in addition to targeting players for the future. A striker would appear unlikely given the presence of Emmanuel Emegha and Danny Welbeck. It will be interesting to watch Emegha's development if given a run of games in the absence of Joao Pedro.
The fact that Xabi Alonso opted for a false nine in three matches prior to Leeds would suggest he believes there are shortcomings in both Emegha and Welbeck's games. It feels more likely that Chelsea will revisit the forward line next summer.
JD: How has Joao Pedro's injury affected how Chelsea has been playing as an overall team, and how has Xabi Alonso had to adapt to it?
James says: The stats are undeniable. Since the start of last season, Chelsea average 1.8 goals per game when Joao Pedro plays, compared to 0.6 when he doesn't. It's quite staggering the difference that the Brazilian seems to make.
Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers look far more potent when they are playing off him. Danny Welbeck initially started in his absence at Brentford. However, he had virtually no impact and appears to have fallen down the pecking order.
Playing Rogers or Pedro Neto as a false-nine has been experimented with but Chelsea have looked blunt without a focal point - though Emmanuel Emegha scored in his first Premier League start which was really encouraging.
Xabi Alonso doesn't tend to give much away but he has described Emegha as being a player with "special" qualities. There's clearly an adaptation period required and Emegha missed a lot of football last season due to injury.
He was also signed prior to Alonso's arrival so it was very much a club signing. Chelsea's season has been derailed by the absence of key players such as Reece James, Joao Pedro and Moises Caicedo.
Alonso needs his big players to step up to ensure they can cope with the casualties - albeit to really key players.
Adam: Why does Alonso not start Welbeck whilst Joao Pedro is injured? Given his experience?
James says: The treatment of Welbeck has been puzzling. He performed really well in the opening two Carabao Cup matches of the season but has featured sparingly since the Brentford defeat.
It was interesting to see how late he was brought on against Tottenham despite Chelsea's need to turn the tide. The 36-year-old (happy birthday today, Danny!) clearly cannot get around the pitch with the same intensity and speed he did when he broke through at Manchester United but that was obvious when he was signed.
Alonso has deflected when asked about Welbeck's lack of minutes but perhaps his inability to press with intensity is one of the main reasons behind him spending more time on the bench than on the pitch.
He's still got a brilliant goalscoring touch - as seen last season at Brighton. He may benefit from more opportunities during a busy December period.
Tim: Should Chelsea be starting Estevao more often? If not, then what should we do with him? Where could we send him on loan if we can't guarantee minutes?
James says: Estevao has only started twice this season - both times at home. He made a huge impact on the pitch and on the supporters when he started in the win against Manchester United. His lack of physical robustness and defensive acumen would appear to be why Xabi Alonso has used him so sparingly.

Sunderland vs Jagiellonia Bialystok. UEFA Europa League Round 1.
Report as Sunderland are held 1-1 by Jagiellonia Bialystok in the Europa League; Black Cats expressed disappointment after some Jagiellonia fans were in attendance in home area at the Stadium of Light; hosts struck early in second half through Timur Tutierov; Kamil Jozwiak soon levelled
Sunderland have expressed their disappointment after some Jagiellonia Bialystok fans were in attendance in home areas during their 1-1 Europa League draw at the Stadium of Light.
A UEFA away supporter ban had been imposed on Jagiellonia for Thursday's fixture on Wearside.
However, in the opening minutes of the match, police and stewards were seen attending to some disruption in a home area in the ground.
A club statement said: "Sunderland AFC is disappointed that a number of Jagiellonia Bialystok supporters were present in home areas of the Stadium of Light during tonight's UEFA Europa League fixture.
"Jagiellonia Bialystok were subject to a UEFA away supporter ban for tonight's Matchday 5 fixture, following a disciplinary sanction imposed by European football's governing body.
"In the build-up to the match, the club had put measures in place in line with this sanction and maintained regular communication with our supporters, Jagiellonia Bialystok and UEFA. Unfortunately, Jagiellonia Bialystok failed to engage and cooperate on this matter.
"We are disappointed that these measures and communications were disregarded by some visiting supporters and will review the circumstances surrounding their entry to the stadium."
As for game itself, Sunderland were left frustrated again in their Europa League campaign after another draw.
The Black Cats enjoyed the best of the first-half chances through Malick Fofana and Nilson Angulo, but the visitors had an opportunity when Robin Roefs saved Kajetan Szmyt's free-kick.
Sunderland struck early in the second half through Timur Tutierov's header, his second goal in the competition, but Kamil Jozwiak levelled only minutes later after capitalising on a mistake at the back.
A point means the Wearsiders stay in the knockout phase play-off places after being held to their second draw from five games in the competition.

Crystal Palace vs Real Sociedad. UEFA Europa League Round 1.
Match report as Thomas Frank earns his first win as Crystal Palace manager; Mamadou Sarr gave Real Sociedad the lead after a dominant opening hour; Jon Martin was sent off and Jean-Philippe Mateta scored from the penalty spot to level; Dwight McNeill score the winner
Thomas Frank earned his first win as Crystal Palace manager, coming from behind to beat Real Sociedad 2-1 in the Europa League.
The Dane lost his opening game to Coventry at the weekend, but saw the heart and fight he will need from his side as they picked up their second win in the competition this season.
For 70 minutes, Sociedad dominated at Selhurst Park, with Dean Henderson needed to make a string of saves. They finally made the breakthrough when Chelsea loanee Mamadou Sarr tapped home from Job Ochieng's cross.
But the game turned out of nowhere as Crystal Palace were awarded a penalty and Jon Martin was sent off. He picked up a second yellow card for holding Jean-Philippe Mateta round the middle, with the striker expertly dispatching the spot kick to level for the Eagles.
The confidence surged in the hosts - backed by the famous atmosphere at Selhurst Park - and it was a well-worked second that put them ahead.
Yeremy Pino's cross was cleared to Jorgen Strand Larsen at the back post, who hit an overhead kick. It wasn't on target, but it did bobble into the six-yard box for the incoming Dwight McNeil, who slid to poke home.
Crystal Palace could have wrapped up the points in a topsy-turvy end after they were awarded another penalty. Carlos Soler was penalised for handball, but Pino's effort was well-saved by Unai Marrero.
The win catapults Crystal Palace into 12th place in the league phase table, just two from the top eight, and gives them a huge boost ahead of another key clash against Hull on Super Sunday . Real Sociedad have slid down into 27th.

90: PENALTY! Crystal Palace are awarded a second penalty for a Soler handball, but Pino has his effort saved.
90+7: SAVE! Henderson pushes away a shot from Oskarsson to keep Sociedad from a late leveller.
Crystal Palace manager Thomas Frank to TNT Sport on if the win can be a turning point: "I surely hope so. You can't underestimate a win, what that gives the group, what they're feeling.
"I think there was more positives than negatives from this performance, but still a lot we need to work on, and to keep working on.
"It's a fantastic feeling to get the win in every aspect here at home and in the circumstances that it's a season that hasn't been living up to everything we expected, so the confidence is maybe not at the highest.
"The ability to come from 1-0 behind and then go to win the game, the mentality and the belief in the players was really good.
"We're playing a very good team, they're fifth in LaLiga, they're very good on the ball. Not everything was perfect in the first half, but the willingness to suffer together and defend together was there, that was good, then we built a little bit more into the second half."
Crystal Palace goalscorer Dwight McNeil to TNT Sport on what Frank has bought to the club: "It's like an energy, a belief. He keeps telling us how good as players we are, but now we're just putting it out on the pitch and we did that tonight.
"We knew it was going to be a tough game but we stuck in there, especially going down 1-0 and then the big man [Mateta] scoring to get us back into the game and then we go on from there."
In response, Frank said: "It's easy to bring energy and the confidence, but what really moves the needle is that you get over the line and get some wins.
"In the last five minutes, I think we all almost were about to get a heart attack because it went both ways, back-to-back. That's also part of the confidence and also we should have controlled that game against 10, but it's football, it's emotions, it's everything."
Analysis from Sky Sports' Charlotte Marsh : "Perhaps one of the most surprising aspects of Crystal Palace this season has been a lack of fight and desire.
"Under Pierre Sage, the team looked disjointed and out of sorts. You did not always see the same determination and sheer-mindedness that has seen the Eagles achieve beyond their wildest dreams over the last few years.
"But we saw that again on Thursday - the Palace of last season, of 'old' perhaps, is still there. To come from behind against a team of Real Sociedad's quality is impressive, and it hinged on one moment. Some fans might say it is about time things started turning in Palace's favour this season.
"They had certainly ridden their luck until that point. Frank very quickly must eradicate the mistakes in and out of possession. Too many sloppy moments allowed Sociedad onto the ball and to have a shot. They were certainly victims of their own lack of precision - Palace might not be so fortunate next time.
"But what the final 20 minutes and result will bring them is a huge boost in confidence that must be channelled towards the Premier League. Frank said in his pre-match press conference that he knows he will be judged on league results and he's right - now it's time to start getting some."

Report from the Europa League clash between Torreense and Celtic at Campo Manuel Marques; Javi Vazquez' own-goal put Celtic in front; Dany Jean levelled before the break; substitute Camilo Duran headed in a late winner for the Hoops; Martin O'Neill's side are up to 25th
Camilo Duran came off the bench to keep Celtic's Europa League hopes alive with a vital win against Torreense.
The Colombian striker peeled away to the back post to meet a cross from fellow substitute James Forrest, guiding a downward header into the net in the 85th minute.
Duran's 15th goal of the season secured a 2-1 victory over the Portuguese second-tier side and moved Celtic on to six points in the Europa League. His latest decisive contribution follows a match-winning double off the bench in the Hoops' comeback victory over Besiktas last time out.
Celtic took the lead in the ninth minute when Javi Vazquez turned Jota's cross into his own net, with Hyun-jun Yang lurking behind him.
However, the Portuguese Cup winners hit back 10 minutes later after some hesitant defending from the visitors. Alex Alfaro rattled the crossbar with a 22-yard effort, but neither Kieran Tierney nor Colby Donovan could deal with the resulting loose balls, allowing Haiti international Dany Jean to volley home the equaliser.
Celtic dominated possession after the break but struggled to create clear-cut opportunities until Duran's late intervention secured all three points.
The Hoops' attention now turns to Hearts on Sunday, live on Sky Sports, as they look to remain top of the Scottish Premiership.
Their next Europa League match is away to Omonia Nicosia on December 10.
